subject: PlatformOps cost comparison & next-step checklist
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@platformops.com>, Jenna Li <jenna.li@platformops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 15:08:00 -0000
Subject: PlatformOps — post-demo cost comparison & next-step checklist

Hi Samir / Jenna,

Thanks again for taking time today — good discussion and helpful context on your volume profile. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can converge on a realistic TCO comparison vs the hyperscaler route you asked about.

Recap (what we heard)
- Daily token volume: ~250M tokens (spiky weekday pattern)
- Typical prompt length: 40–120 tokens; avg. response length ~120 tokens
- Expected prefix reuse/cache hit target: ~35% (system prompts + agent templates)
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 450ms for interactive workflows
- Security requirements: SOC-like logs, VPC option considered

High-level Redwood vs hyperscaler framing (assumptions in attached matrix)
- Redwood hosted baseline: per-1M tokens estimate assumes dynamic batching, prefix KV caching, quantized rtx-optimized model variant.
- Hyperscaler managed endpoint: assume single-instance scaling, no automatic prefix cache, higher per-inference overhead for small requests.
- Key knobs: effective cache hit rate, batching slot size (affects throughput), and model variant (FP16 vs int8).

Proposed empirical tests (to produce apples-to-apples economics)
1) 1M-token run with live batching (simulate your weekday spike pattern) — measure tokens/s, avg/95th latency, and effective GPU utilization.
2) Cache-hit sensitivity sweep — run synthetic workload at 0%, 25%, 50% cache hit to show delta on per-1M token cost.
3) Latency SLO validation — run 15-minute orthogonal test at target concurrency to capture p95 and tail behavior.
4) Cost tie-out — combine real measured throughput with our reserved/dedicated vs hosted pricing and hyperscaler quotes you provide.

Immediate asks from you
- Can you share a sample production trace or a small anonymized corpus (5–10k prompts) so we can emulate real prefix distributions?
- Any hyperscaler quote or documented per-inference SKU you want us to include in the matrix?
- Do you want us to run the tests on Redwood hosted first, then mirror to Dedicated / Private if numbers look good?

Attachment: redwood-hyperscaler-matrix-v1.pdf (static assumptions + quick sensitivity chart), 1M-token-econ-projection.xlsx (workbook with cost model).

Proposed timeline
- Share artifacts by EOD Wed (Jan 27) -> we run quick hosted tests Thurs/Fri -> share test artifacts Mon next week.

Next steps
- Samir / Jenna to share sample trace and any hyperscaler quotes.
- Ben / Rishi and I will kick off the hosted run once we get the corpus.

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite for a short 30-min test kickoff if you’re ok with the plan.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Olga,

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with our takeaways. Quick answers inline:

Samir

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 09:21:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: PlatformOps — post-demo cost comparison & next-step checklist

Thanks — quick draft numbers below (ballpark; we'll refine after the hosted run). These assume: quantized model variant, batching enabled in continuous-batching mode, and average response length 120 tokens.

Per-1M token estimated cost (hosted)
- 0% cache hit: $32 per 1M tokens
- 25% cache hit: $25 per 1M tokens
- 50% cache hit: $19 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- These include GPU time + infra overhead but exclude long-term audit log storage/evidence costs. For retention: standard 90-day audit logs add approx $0.8 per 1M tokens; longer retention or S3 Glacier adds more.
- Hyperscaler quote (from Samir): their blended per-1M equivalent (using their instance math) is roughly $38–45 per 1M tokens for small interactive SLOs because their managed endpoint doesn't benefit from prefix KV caching and batching efficiency at those prompt lengths.

Next actions I will take this week:
- Produce a CSV with cost rows for 0/25/50% cache hit and a simple formula so Samir can drop their actual instance hourly numbers to compare.
- Work with Rishi to finalize the hosted test harness and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and GPU utilization.

If these ballparks look directionally right to you Olga, I'll attach the CSV to the Drive and we can run.

Ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
